title: Reinterpret Section 230 to narrow tech platforms' legal immunity
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should issue an order interpreting Section 230 to remove broad legal protections that courts have read into the law, making clear its protections apply more narrowly when platforms remove content.
quote: The FCC should issue an order that interprets Section 230 in a way that eliminates the expansive, non-textual immunities that courts have read into the statute.
contested: Chapter notes some conservative contributors oppose regulating platforms' content moderation

title: Impose transparency rules on Big Tech platforms
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should require large tech platforms to disclose specific terms of service, similar to broadband transparency rules, and bar actions that go against those terms.
quote: Impose transparency rules on Big Tech. Today, Big Tech offers a black box.
contested: Chapter notes some conservative contributors oppose regulating platforms' content moderation

title: Require Big Tech to offer an appeals process for takedowns
proposal: The chapter says large tech platforms should be required to offer a clear appeals process so users can challenge takedowns or other actions that break the platform's stated rules.
quote: Big Tech should be required to offer a transparent appeals process that allows for the challenging of pretextual takedowns
contested: Chapter notes some conservative contributors oppose regulating platforms' content moderation

title: Support legislation to overhaul Section 230
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should work with Congress on deeper Section 230 changes so internet companies cannot remove protected speech while keeping Section 230 protections, focusing on dominant general-use platforms.
quote: Support legislation that scraps Section 230's current approach. The FCC should work with Congress on more fundamental Section 230 reforms
contested: Chapter notes some conservative contributors oppose regulating platforms' content moderation

title: Apply anti-discrimination rules to Big Tech, including hosting firms
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should work with Congress to apply anti-discrimination rules to Big Tech, including behind-the-scenes hosting and security companies, such as by barring discrimination against core political viewpoints.
quote: the FCC should work with Congress to ensure that antidiscrimination provisions are applied to Big Tech
contested: Chapter notes some conservative contributors oppose regulating platforms' content moderation

title: Let users choose their own content filters and fact checkers
proposal: The chapter says the FCC and Congress should create rules that give users more control online, such as letting them choose their own content filters and fact checkers, if any.
quote: One idea is to empower consumers to choose their own content filters and fact checkers, if any.

title: Strengthen protections keeping young children off social media
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should work with Congress on stronger protections to keep young children from using social media sites despite age limits.
quote: The FCC should also work with Congress to ensure stronger protections against young children accessing social media sites

title: Make Big Tech pay into the Universal Service Fund
proposal: The chapter says Congress should require Big Tech companies to contribute to the FCC's roughly $9 billion Universal Service Fund, which is now paid for by charges on phone bills.
quote: Congress should require Big Tech companies to start contributing an appropriate amount.
contested: Chapter notes some conservatives instead want Congress to revisit the whole fund through regular appropriations

title: Ban TikTok if its national security review stays unresolved
proposal: The chapter says that if the Treasury's review of TikTok stays unresolved or TikTok is allowed to keep operating, a new Administration should ban the app on national security grounds.
quote: a new Administration should ban the application on national security grounds.

title: Regularly update the FCC's list of banned risky equipment
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should create a more regular and timely process for adding companies tied to China's surveillance state to its "Covered List" of banned communications equipment and services.
quote: a new Administration should create a more regular and timely process for reviewing entities with ties to the CCP's surveillance state.

title: Close loophole letting banned Chinese carriers serve U.S. data centers
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should stop banned companies like China Telecom from offering similar services on an "unregulated" basis, for example by barring regulated carriers from connecting with insecure providers.
quote: One way to do so would be for the FCC to prohibit any regulated carrier from interconnecting with an insecure provider.

title: Publish a list of FCC license holders owned by foreign adversaries
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should publish a list of all license holders that are more than 10 percent owned by governments of China, Russia, Iran, Syria, or North Korea.
quote: the FCC should compile and publish a list of all entities that hold FCC authorizations, licenses, or other grants of authority

title: Fully fund "rip and replace" of Huawei and ZTE equipment
proposal: The chapter says the program that pays providers to remove and replace Huawei and ZTE equipment, about $3 billion short, should be fully funded, starting with unused COVID-era emergency funds.
quote: A new Administration should ensure that the program is fully funded and should look first at repurposing and applying unused COVID-era emergency funds

title: Launch a "Clean Standards" initiative against Chinese influence
proposal: The chapter says the U.S. should launch a broad initiative to counter China's influence over technology and telecommunications standard-setting, building on the earlier Clean Networks program.
quote: It is vital that the United States meet this threat with a comprehensive clean standards initiative.

title: Stop U.S. companies from helping China's AI development
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should create a plan to stop U.S. entities, including cloud computing providers, from directly or indirectly helping China's AI goals.
quote: it is time for an Administration to put in place a comprehensive plan that aims to stop U.S. entities from directly or indirectly contributing to China's malign AI goals.

title: Create a national spectrum strategy to free airwaves for wireless
proposal: The chapter says the FCC and the Administration should create a national plan identifying airwaves that can be freed for commercial wireless use, with an aggressive timeline.
quote: the FCC and a new Administration should work together to develop a national spectrum strategy

title: Set up a federal spectrum coordination process
proposal: The chapter says the White House should work with Congress to create a process for coordinating airwave use between commercial wireless companies and federal agencies, citing the 2021-2022 5G and aviation dispute.
quote: The White House should work with Congress to establish a spectrum coordination process that will work for both commercial and federal users.

title: Cap state and local fees and delays for wired broadband permits
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should consider limiting the fees state and local governments can charge to review wired infrastructure applications and setting time limits on their decisions.
quote: imposing limits on the fees that local and state governments can charge for reviewing those wireline applications

title: Speed broadband permits on federal lands
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should push agencies that manage federal lands, such as the Bureau of Land Management and Forest Service, to review and decide on internet infrastructure projects on time.
quote: so a new Administration should redouble efforts to require timely reviews and final actions by agencies with jurisdiction over federal lands

title: Approve new internet satellite launches faster
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should speed up its review and approval of applications to launch new low-earth orbit internet satellites like StarLink and Kuiper.
quote: The FCC should expedite its work to support this new technology by acting more quickly in its review and approval of applications to launch new satellites.

title: Target broadband funds to unserved areas; end overbuilding
proposal: The chapter says agencies handling broadband money should send it to communities without adequate internet, and the government should stop funding new networks where high-speed service already exists.
quote: instruct the various departments and agencies that are administering broadband infrastructure funds to direct those resources to communities without adequate Internet infrastructure

title: Adopt a national broadband strategy with spending oversight
proposal: The chapter says the Administration should bring new oversight to broadband spending and adopt a national strategy to coordinate more than 100 federal broadband programs run by 15 agencies.
quote: A new Administration needs to bring fresh oversight to this spending and put a national strategy in place

title: Review FCC broadband programs, including the Universal Service Fund
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should review its broadband programs, including parts of the Universal Service Fund, to avoid duplication, improve efficiency, and save money.
quote: the next Administration should ask the FCC to launch a review of its existing broadband programs, including the different components of the USF

title: Eliminate many FCC media ownership rules
proposal: The chapter says many older FCC rules, including many media ownership rules and universal service requirements, should be eliminated because the market now has more competition.
quote: These include many of the FCC's media ownership rules, which can have the effect of restricting investment and competition

title: Do a top-to-bottom review and repeal outdated FCC rules
proposal: The chapter says the FCC should review all its regulations and rescind any that are overly burdensome or outdated.
quote: The FCC should engage in a serious top-to-bottom review of its regulations and take steps to rescind any that are overly cumbersome or outdated.
